title: KV cache probe & quantization quicklog
content:
Quick scratchpad: experimenting with KV cache behavior and cheap quantized 4-bit variants. Notes are messy — just my running log and TODOs. Aim is to understand how prefix caching interacts with batching/latency and whether int4 quantization regresses on instruction-following for our typical prompt shapes.

Context/goal:
- Workload: short interactive assistant calls (system+user ~ 40-120 tokens), then a single multi-turn continuation (150-400 tokens). SLO: p95 latency < 250ms for generation start on Dedicated pool.
- Hypothesis: prefix/KV reuse will give large per-token cost saving but only if KV cache lookup overhead < 10ms; quantized int4 models might increase compute time per token but reduce memory pressure for larger batches. Need numbers.

Quick experiment plan (priority order):
1) KV probe: same prompt repeated across requests, measure extra latency for first request vs subsequent cached requests (no model change).
2) KV + batching: send N concurrent requests (N=1,4,8) with same prefix and measure throughput & p95.
3) Quantized int4 candidates: run same eval prompts on fp16 baseline, q4_0, q4_1 variants, compare avg response time and semantic fidelity (ROUGE-L on canned tests + human pass/fail).
4) Combined: int4 + KV + batching to see interaction (buffering overhead, cache eviction patterns).

Run log (raw)
2026-02-18 09:22 - start KV probe (dev-dedicated-1):
- model: redwood-open-7b-fp16 (baseline)
- prompt: system short instruction + user ask for 3 bullet suggestions (avg token len 68)
Commands used: 
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Payloads: first request includes full prompt, second request sends same prompt but with "use_kv_cache": true and previously cached context id. (simulated via local key)

Results (local timestamps):
- first request latency (time to first token): 210ms
- cached request latency: 78ms
- delta: ~132ms saved (63% reduction)
Notes: double-check clock sync between client and server, but relative difference consistent across 6 repeats. p95 for cached ~ 92ms.

2026-02-18 11:05 - KV + concurrent requests
Setup: send 1,4,8 concurrent identical requests (same prefix), Observe how runtime merges requests into same KV cache entry (continuous batching).
- N=1: throughput ~ 12 tokens/s, p95 start 210ms (baseline)
- N=4: aggregated throughput ~ 34 tokens/s (not linear), per-request p95 start 240ms for cold, cached ones ~ 95ms
- N=8: throughput ~ 60 tokens/s, but observed tail latency increase for some requests (p99 > 1s), likely queueing in batching window.
Notes: batching tradeoff — need adaptive batch windows. Consider per-model batching cap + latency window at 60ms to protect p95.

2026-02-19 10:00 - Quantization sweep (same eval set of 120 prompts):
Models: redwood-open-7b-fp16 (baseline), redwood-open-7b-q4_0, redwood-open-7b-q4_1
Metrics collected: avg latency start (ms), avg generation throughput (tok/s), automatic accuracy proxy (ROUGE-L vs reference), human sanity-check pass rate (10 sample prompts)
Results summary (median of 3 runs each):
- fp16: start 210ms, tok/s 12, ROUGE-L 0.62, human pass 9/10
- q4_0: start 250ms, tok/s 10, ROUGE-L 0.55, human pass 6/10 (hallucinations on numeric lists)
- q4_1: start 235ms, tok/s 11, ROUGE-L 0.59, human pass 8/10
Notes: q4_1 looks promising — small latency hit but acceptable quality. q4_0 too lossy for our instruction style. Must run larger eval before deciding. Also check memory pressure numbers (q4 models reduce GPU memory footprint by ~2.6x in this toy env).

2026-02-19 14:30 - Combined int4 + KV + small batch windows
- Use redwood-open-7b-q4_1 with KV enabled, batch window 50ms, max_batch 8.
Observed:
- cached start latency: 95-110ms (close to fp16 cached numbers), throughput up ~ +20% due to smaller mem footprint
- rare decoding glitches: repeated token occasionally (seen 3x in 400 requests). Might be quantization + caching edge case. Need to reproduce deterministically.

Small checklist / TODOs (next actions):
- [ ] Reproduce cached token-repeat with deterministic seed and smaller example. Add to GitHub issue and attach logs.
- [ ] Increase eval set to 2k prompts across our top-10 templates, measure q4_1 fidelity + ROUGE/BERScore.
- [ ] Run 24h soak on Dedicated pool with q4_1 + KV to measure cache eviction patterns under steady workload. Collect per-request cache hit ratio time-series.
- [ ] Add instrumentation: per-request KV lookup time and per-token kernel time (want KV lookup < 10ms median).
- [ ] Try alternate quant configs: q4_2 if available, and a per-layer mixed-precision (last n layers fp16) to see fidelity vs memory tradeoff.
- [ ] Check interplay with function-calling structured output (we saw more hallucinations under q4_0 when output included code blocks).

Prompt set samples (for eval / reproducibility):
- Template A (assistant tips): "System: You are concise. User: Give 5 quick ways to reduce cloud inference cost for a web app."
- Template B (code completion): "System: You are an expert Python dev. User: Complete this function to compute running median for sliding window. Code: <snippet>"
- Template C (multi-turn): System instruction then 2 user turns where second turn references data from first. Designed to test KV persistence across turns (prefix length ~ 120 tokens).

Quick notes on instrumentation I added locally:
- rudimentary script (kv_probe.py) logs: request_id, start_ts, first_token_ts, kv_hit, kv_lookup_ms, batch_size, model_variant, seed
- sample log line: "r1234,2026-02-18T09:22:11.234Z,2026-02-18T09:22:11.444Z,true,6.7,1,redwood-open-7b-fp16,42"

Potential risks / unknowns: 
- cache consistency: when rolling deploys with model binary changes, ensure KV invalidation happens correctly. Otherwise cached embeddings/KV could map to wrong kernel layout and produce bad output. Need a test where model variant id changes but we reuse cached prefix (should be blocked).
- quantization edge cases with control tokens / stop sequences — observed one case where stop token detection delayed and repeated one token. Could be quantization error in softmax logits.

Notes for writeup to product/infra team:
- preliminary result: KV cache gives ~60% startup latency reduction for identical prefixes; q4_1 gives modest memory & cost wins with acceptable quality on short instruction tasks. Recommend conservative rollout: q4_1 behind canary + per-route quality monitoring (open/closed evals).
- recommend infra changes: expose per-request kv_lookup_ms and kv_hit boolean in request logs; add a cache-invalidation API for model variant changes.

Random thoughts / open questions: 
- Could we implement a lightweight cache fingerprint that is model-variant aware to avoid silent reuse? E.g., prefix_hash + model_abi_version -> only reuse if match.
- For PLG usage patterns (lots of short identical prompts), maybe pre-warm common prefixes for new tenants to avoid cold starts. How to select warm prefixes? Use top-K by frequency per tenant.

Attachments/links: see linked_artifacts above. Will push kv_probe.py and sample logs to github:repo/serve-infra/pull/1834 (WIP).

End of scratchpad for now. Will clean up and produce short summary memo if numbers hold after extended eval.

Priya
